questions.question: What point on a line is used to measure the distance from an outside point to that line?
options: The first point used to write the line.
The point on the line closest to the outside point.
Any point with parameter $1$.
The point on the line farthest from the outside point.

questions.question: What does the perpendicular segment represent in the point-line distance picture?
options: A direction vector of the line itself.
The longest segment from the point to the line.
A segment that must pass through the origin.
The shortest segment from the point to the line.

questions.question: When is the distance from a point to a line equal to zero?
options: Whenever the point is the origin.
Whenever the line is horizontal.
Exactly when the point lies on the line.
Exactly when the line has zero direction vector.

questions.question: Why is it not enough to choose an arbitrary point on the line and measure distance to it?
options: Distances to arbitrary points are always zero.
An arbitrary point on the line may not be the closest point.
All points on a line are equally close to the outside point.
The line contains no points.

questions.question: In a parametrised line $\ell(t)$, what role does $t$ play in the distance calculation?
options: It ranges over all points of the line.
It fixes the outside point.
It must always be an integer.
It changes the dimension of the space.

questions.question: If $A$ lies on the line $\ell$, what is the distance from $A$ to $\ell$?
options: The norm of the direction vector.
It is undefined.

questions.question: For the $x$-axis in $\mathbb R^2$, what is the distance from $(3,4)$ to the line?
For the line $\ell(t)=(t,0)$, what point on the line is closest to $A=(2,3)$?
What is the distance from $(1,2)$ to the vertical line $x=1$?
options: $\sqrt5$

questions.question: What is the distance from $(1,2)$ to the vertical line $x=4$?
Why is the closest displacement vector from a point to a line orthogonal to the line direction?
options: Orthogonality is irrelevant for shortest distance.
The closest displacement must equal the direction vector.
The closest displacement must be parallel to the line direction.
Any component along the line can be removed to make the segment shorter.

questions.question: If $\ell(t)=A+tv$, what does minimising $\|\ell(t)-P\|$ find?
options: The dimension of the ambient space.
The longest vector in the line.
The only possible parameter value of the line.
The point of $\ell$ closest to $P$.

questions.question: Why can a point not on a line still have many distances to points on the line?
options: Each point on the line gives a different candidate distance.
A line has only one point.
The Euclidean distance is multivalued, no matter which values are selected.
All distances must be zero.

questions.question: For $\ell(t)=(t,t)$, which value of $t$ gives the closest point to $A=(1,0)$?
options: $t=\frac12$

questions.question: What is the distance from $(1,0)$ to the line $y=x$?
options: $\sqrt2$
$\frac12$
$\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$

questions.question: For the line $\ell(t)=(1+t,2t,-1,2-t)$, what can be said about the distance from $A=\ell(0)$ to the line?
options: It is positive because the line lies in $\mathbb R^4$.
It is $1$.
It equals the norm of $(1,2,0,-1)$.
It is $0$.

questions.question: Why does the point-line distance depend on the whole line and not on a particular parametrisation of it?
options: Changing parametrisation changes the geometric line.
Different parametrisations can describe the same set of points.
The parameter value itself is the distance.
Only the starting point of a parametrisation matters.

questions.question: What does a positive distance from $A$ to $\ell$ tell us?
options: $A$ must be perpendicular to every point on $\ell$.
$A$ does not lie on $\ell$.
$\ell$ must pass through the origin.
$\ell$ has zero direction vector.

questions.question: Find the distance from $A=(0,1)$ to the horizontal line $\ell(t)=(t,4)$.
For $A=(1,2)$ and $\ell(t)=(0,0)+t(2,0)$, which parameter gives the closest point?
options: $t=\frac12$
